mcp.intro: Expose the connections you choose below to an AI coding tool (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity, Codex, …) over the Model Context Protocol — opt-in per connection, with a per-connection write policy (read-only by default).
mcp.sharedIdsHint: Which connections are exposed is a decision about this machine: it is kept out of exports and never changed by a shared-origin sync, so each teammate ticks their own. The snippet carries no connection ids, so it is the same on every machine and you only paste it once.
mcp.bulkPolicyNoop: They were already set to that
mcp.bulkPolicyFullBody: Full access lets an AI client change data AND schema on these connections — CREATE, ALTER, DROP included. Every write is recorded in the app's MCP audit log, but nothing asks again at the time.
mcp.unavailable: Not found — this build wasn't installed from a packaged release, so the connector isn't bundled.
mcp.noConnections: No saved connections yet — add one first.
mcp.writePolicyHint: Write access is per connection. “Read-only” allows only reads; “Data” allows row changes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE); “Full” also allows schema changes (CREATE/DROP/ALTER). Changes take effect without restarting the AI client. The client still asks you to approve each action, and every write is recorded in mcp-audit.log next to your profiles.
mcp.exposureSaveError: Couldn't save which connections are exposed.
mcp.noBinaryHint: The connector binary wasn't found, so there's nothing to point a client at.
mcp.nothingExposedHint: No connections are ticked yet — the connector will start with nothing to reach. Tick one above; it takes effect without restarting the AI client.

pulse.intro: How often Pulse samples a connection's vital signs into its on-disk history, how long that history is kept, and which connections it watches — opt-in per connection, off by default.

historyIntervalSecs.label: Sample every
historyIntervalSecs.desc: Seconds between history ticks for each connection with Pulse enabled. This is the read that actually costs a round trip against the server — the dock panel's live view polls independently and is not affected.

retentionDays.label: Keep history for
retentionDays.desc: Days a history point survives before it is pruned. Samples older than 48 hours are downsampled to one point per 5 minutes first; that step is not adjustable.

maxDiskMb.label: Disk budget
maxDiskMb.desc: Soft cap on pulse.db's size, in megabytes. 0 disables it. A safety valve on top of the retention window above, not a replacement for tuning it.

sampleWhenMinimized.label: Sample while minimised
sampleWhenMinimized.desc: Keep ticking while HuginnDB's window is minimised. Off trades a gap in the history for zero server load whenever the app isn't on screen.

childIdleTtl.desc: Seconds a database view may go untouched before its pool is closed. It reopens by itself the next time you use it. 0 disables this.

bridgeIdleTtl.label: Close idle connector connections after
bridgeIdleTtl.desc: Seconds a connection the MCP connector opened may go untouched before it is closed. Nothing in the app shows these, and the connector reopens one by itself on its next call. 0 keeps them until the app exits.

operationTimeout.label: Operation timeout
operationTimeout.desc: Seconds a single schema read may take — listing databases and tables, describing a relation, the liveness ping. Never a query you run. A server that needs longer is better set on its own connection, where the value travels with it.

keepalive.label: Keepalive interval
keepalive.desc: Seconds between liveness pings. The ping holds one connection open per connection so the next click is instant and dropped connections are detected early. 0 turns it off.

connections.footnote: Limits apply when a pool is opened; pools already open keep what they were granted. Reconnect to apply them immediately. When a server's allowance is spent, opening a database view closes the one you used least recently rather than failing.

mcpBridge.label: Share pools with the MCP connector
mcpBridge.desc: Let a running huginndb-mcp sidecar use this app's connections instead of opening its own, so the whole machine shares one budget per server — and its activity appears in the Console as it happens. Opens a token-protected listener on localhost. Off by default.

ai.intro: Where the assistant's model runs, how much that endpoint is trusted with your data, and which connections it may read. Off by default, and nothing here reaches a database until a connection is enabled below.

enabled.label: Enable the AI panel
enabled.desc: Off on every existing install. While it is off, HuginnDB makes no request to any inference endpoint.

baseUrl.label: Endpoint
baseUrl.desc: An OpenAI-compatible base URL — Ollama, LM Studio, llama-server, vLLM, or a cloud provider. Plain http is allowed on purpose: one GPU box serving the office LAN (http://ai-internal:11434/v1) is the deployment this feature is built around. Every scheme but http and https is refused.

model.label: Model
model.desc: The model id to ask for. Test the endpoint below and this becomes a list — unless the server does not publish one, which is normal for llama-server.

trust.label: Endpoint trust
trust.desc: Whether this endpoint is your own infrastructure. You declare it; HuginnDB never infers it from a hostname, because DNS is not a security boundary. A trusted endpoint may read rows. An untrusted one gets table and column names, types, indexes and EXPLAIN output only — unless a connection below opts in.
trust.looksLocal: This endpoint looks local (loopback or a private network) but is marked as a third party, so rows are withheld unless a connection opts in below.
trust.looksRemote: This endpoint does not look local, and it is marked as your own infrastructure. Rows from every reachable connection may be sent to it.

mode.label: Mode
mode.desc: Assisted makes one model call with context HuginnDB assembles itself, and works on a small local model. Agent runs a real tool-call loop and needs a model that emits reliable tool calls.
mode.notToolCapable: This model does not emit reliable tool calls, so agent mode will not work with it. Assisted mode is available.

maxContextRows.label: Row budget
maxContextRows.desc: How many rows one tool reply may put into the model's context. Much smaller than a page of the grid on purpose: a context window is a tighter budget than a screen, and a model reasons worse as it fills. Capped at 1000.

reasoningEffort.label: Thinking
reasoningEffort.desc: How much a thinking model should reason before answering, sent as reasoning_effort. Nearly every current local model is a thinking model, and left alone it spends a paragraph of reasoning before the first useful token — pick None for a local model in assisted mode. Automatic sends nothing at all, which is the only setting guaranteed not to be rejected: OpenAI refuses the field outright on a model that does not reason.

requestTimeoutSecs.label: Idle timeout
requestTimeoutSecs.desc: Seconds a request may go without receiving a byte before it is abandoned. Not a total budget — a slow model answering correctly is not a broken one.

ai.keyHint: Only needed for a cloud provider; every local server ignores it. Stored in the OS keychain and keyed to this endpoint's host, so changing the endpoint above cannot send this key somewhere else. HuginnDB never shows it again.
ai.keyReplacePlaceholder: Paste a key to replace the stored one
ai.probeUntested: Not tested yet. The check asks the endpoint which models it serves and makes one small tool call, so it costs a real request.
ai.probeDisabled: Enable the panel above to test the endpoint.
ai.connectionsHint: Two separate decisions per connection. Reach is whether the assistant can see it at all — off means it cannot be named, by name or by id. Rows is whether row data may be sent to an untrusted endpoint; metadata never depends on it.
ai.noConnections: No saved connections yet — add one first.
ai.rowsTooltip: Allow this connection's rows to be sent to the endpoint. Metadata is sent either way.
ai.rowsTrustedTooltip: The endpoint is marked as your own infrastructure, so rows are allowed regardless. To withhold this connection entirely, turn its reach off.
ai.mcpAlternative: Already paying for Claude or ChatGPT? Those subscriptions cannot be spent through HuginnDB. The sanctioned path is the MCP connector, which lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor read your databases through HuginnDB — at the cost of your data going to that vendor.
ai.notesHint: What this database's schema does not say: which codes a column uses, which of two similar tables is the live one, what it is for. Sent with every question about this connection.
ai.notesPlaceholder: cfg_* is one row per tenant. status uses the legacy codes: 0 pending, 1 live, 9 archived. Ignore log_old — nothing writes to it since 2024.
ai.notesNone: Enable a connection above to give it notes.

policy.brokenHint: The policy could not be applied, so no connection can be read or written — by you or by the AI. Ask your administrator to fix it.
policy.unmanagedConnections: Connections the policy does not name

policy.humanGuardrail: For people, the app applies the policy as a guardrail: someone who holds a database password can still use another client. A database user per person, with matching grants, is what closes that.

grants.title: Database permissions for a role
grants.description: The GRANTs (or MongoDB role) a policy role needs on one server, so the database itself enforces what the role allows for each person's own database user. HuginnDB never runs this script: review it, then run it as an administrator.
grants.noConnection: Connect to the server with your administrator account first: the script is built from its catalog.

1_32_0.tagline: The documentation viewer is rebuilt with search, connections hold up better against server limits, SSH tunnels reconnect on their own, and the MCP connector no longer stops when HuginnDB is closed.

documentationViewer.title: The documentation viewer matches Preferences
documentationViewer.body: It opens on a home page, searches the text of every guide, follows your reading with an On this page column and carries on with Previous / Next. Each Preferences section with a guide now has a Read the guide button.

connectionCounts.title: See how many connections are really open
connectionCounts.body: Settings → Connections shows open against reserved for each server, and a second connection to the same server now reserves half of what is left instead of five, so three profiles fit where two did. At the limit, unused database views are closed before anything is refused.

tunnelsReconnect.title: SSH tunnels and lost connections recover by themselves
tunnelsReconnect.body: Tunnels send their own keepalive and reconnect the next time they are used. A lost connection is retried twice before alerting and its warning clears when it answers again. A query after a long pause no longer waits 30 seconds and blames the server.

disconnectAndClose.title: Disconnecting is immediate and nothing is left open
disconnectAndClose.body: The tree, tabs and other windows update at once while the connection closes in the background. Closing a window or quitting HuginnDB now closes its connections properly, and the same connection is never opened twice at once.

mcpFallback.title: The MCP connector survives a closed HuginnDB
mcpFallback.body: With the bridge on, the connector falls back to its own connections when the app is closed, keeps looking for the app to switch back, and reconnects before the first request after a restart instead of failing it.

schemaTree.title: A schema tree that tells you what it is doing
schemaTree.body: Placeholder rows and a spinner while a database loads, a Retry button on a failed read instead of endless retries, and MongoDB collections that appear straight away over SSH, with counts and sizes filling in after.

1_31_0.tagline: Work in two environments at once, deleting a row tells you why it was refused, and a MongoDB script with one call per line finally runs every call.

environmentNewWindow.title: Open an environment in a new window
environmentNewWindow.body: Right-click an environment in the rail and choose Open environment in new window to work in it beside your current one, without leaving the layout you just arranged. It reconnects that environment's connections and writes nothing.

deleteRowReason.title: Deleting a row explains a refusal
deleteRowReason.body: When other tables still reference the row, the confirmation stays open with the reason and names the tables that point at it, instead of the click seeming to do nothing.

mongoLinePerStatement.title: One MongoDB call per line, each with its own result
mongoLinePerStatement.body: As in mongosh, the semicolon is optional: a line break ends a statement when nothing is left open. Three countDocuments on three lines now give three result tabs and three Run lenses instead of one.

mongoTrailingRefused.title: Extra statements are refused, not dropped
mongoTrailingRefused.body: Through MCP run_query and the AI panel, a statement followed by another used to run the first and report success. It now fails with an error, so nothing is silently skipped.

1_30_0.tagline: HuginnDB keeps itself up to date, and so does the MCP connector your AI tool uses — installed once, with nothing to do per computer after that. Plus one title bar instead of two.

silentUpdates.title: Updates install themselves
silentUpdates.body: On Windows a scheduled task checks at sign-in and once a day and installs quietly, even if HuginnDB is never opened. It waits while the app is open, and Settings → About → Background updates shows what is in force or turns it off.

extensionUpdates.title: The Claude Desktop extension updates with the app
extensionUpdates.body: The extension now hands every session to the connector installed with HuginnDB, so new tools reach your AI tool with each update. Install it once more with this version and never again.

unifiedTitleBar.title: One title bar instead of two
unifiedTitleBar.body: The native caption is gone on Windows and Linux: HuginnDB's own bar carries minimise, maximise and close, and gives the row back. It still drags, double-clicks to maximise and snaps.

jumpList.title: Recent connections on the taskbar
jumpList.body: Right-click HuginnDB on the taskbar to open a recent connection or a new window. Only names and engines are listed, never hosts or passwords.

1_29_0.tagline: HuginnDB for organizations: one managed policy decides what each person and their AI may reach, the database enforces it, and it is edited in the app. Plus a Preferences dialog you can search.

managedPolicy.title: A managed policy for people and their AI
managedPolicy.body: An administrator gives each OS account a role, and each role rules per server what is visible and whether it may select, insert, update, delete, change schema or monitor. The AI is held to it strictly and never learns the names of what it cannot reach; in the app every command checks it, and what a role does not allow is shown locked, with the reason.

personalDbUser.title: Each person signs in as their own database user
personalDbUser.body: A rule can pin the user a person connects as ("erp_{user}"), or a person picks their own on a shared connection, kept on this machine only. Settings → Policy → Generate grants writes the GRANT script (or MongoDB role) each role needs, so the database itself enforces the policy.

policyEditor.title: Edit the policy in HuginnDB, not by hand
policyEditor.body: Settings → Policy → Edit policy opens it as a form with the JSON one pane away. Every change is checked by the parser that applies it, View as shows what any account would get, and a save keeps a .bak and never overwrites someone else's change.

readOnlyEnforced.title: Read-only means read-only
readOnlyEnforced.body: A WITH carrying a DELETE, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and a MongoDB $out / $merge were classified as reads; now they get the tier of what they do. And a read the AI sends runs inside a read-only transaction on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite, so anything the classifier misses fails on the server.

preferences.title: Preferences, regrouped and searchable
preferences.body: The rail is grouped, a search box finds any of the ~65 settings in either language, and every setting moved off its default carries a dot and a one-click reset. Across the app, every button now has a visible edge, on imported themes too.

findEverywhere.title: Ctrl+F finds in whatever you are looking at
findEverywhere.body: In a table tab it goes to that table's filter, otherwise to the schema tree's, and in Preferences to the settings search. Inside a query editor the editor's own find still wins.

mongoInsertTypes.title: MongoDB inserts keep their types
mongoInsertTypes.body: A document inserted or duplicated from the grid was written with every field as a string — a Long 5 became "5". Each field now keeps its type, and an empty collection finally offers Insert for its first document.

1_28_0.tagline: The advanced filter grows into a query panel under the toolbar — choose the fields, write the filter by hand, sort, force an index and read the plan, all with the rows still in view.

queryPanel.title: The advanced filter is now a query panel
queryPanel.body: The filter button opens a Query section between the toolbar and the rows instead of a dialog, so the data stays visible while you shape it. Nothing reaches the server until Apply (or Ctrl/⌘+Enter), and a draft that differs from what is applied says so. Filter and sort chips get a row of their own that wraps instead of folding.

handWrittenFilter.title: Write the filter by hand, and see the query it runs
handWrittenFilter.body: Next to the conditions, type an expression — a WHERE condition on SQL, a filter document on MongoDB — and it is ANDed with the rest. A Result line shows the exact statement the browse will run, with Copy and Open in editor to take it elsewhere.

projection.title: Choose which fields come back
projection.body: Columns on SQL, Projection (Include / Exclude) on MongoDB: the server only sends what you pick, so wide JSON or text columns stop travelling on every page. The key always comes back so rows stay editable, and Export query results now writes exactly what the grid shows — filters, sort and projection.

sortEverywhere.title: Sort from anywhere, in both view modes
sortEverywhere.body: A Sort button in the toolbar builds a multi-level sort, sort chips show it and flip its direction, and every field in the list view has a menu to sort or filter by it — nested MongoDB paths included. The footer also gained Go to row.

explainAndHints.title: Explain, collation and index hints
explainAndHints.body: The panel's Advanced row sets a collation and forces an index per browse, in each engine's own syntax. Explain reads the plan of the draft without running it — the engine's own EXPLAIN, or MongoDB's queryPlanner.

fkPickerRefresh.title: The foreign-key picker stays current
fkPickerRefresh.body: Renaming a key in the referenced table no longer leaves the picker offering the old value until restart: it still opens instantly with the list it had, then re-reads the referenced table and swaps in the fresh one.

1_27_0.tagline: The table's own CREATE statement one click away, a drop dialog that tells you what depends on the table, and a timeout that waits as long as your server needs.

createStatement.title: Copy a table's CREATE statement
createStatement.body: The structure editor has a new CREATE section showing the definition exactly as the server stores it — engine, charset, comments and partitions on MySQL/MariaDB; indexes and triggers on SQLite — with a Copy button. It is left out on PostgreSQL and SQL Server rather than rebuilt incompletely.

dropTableReferences.title: See what references a table before dropping it
dropTableReferences.body: The drop dialog now lists every foreign key on another table that points at this one, as table (columns) → constraint, before you confirm — instead of the server refusing the drop with an error that often names no table at all.

operationTimeout.title: An operation timeout you can set
operationTimeout.body: The 20-second limit on listing databases and tables is now a default: change it in Settings → Connections, or override it per connection for that server with hundreds of databases. Queries you run yourself stay unbounded, as before.

mongoFilterTypes.title: MongoDB filters say which type they compare
mongoFilterTypes.body: Each condition can pin its value type — Auto, String, Number, Long, Boolean, Date or ObjectId — and chips print it the shell's way. The filter also takes a field's type from the page on screen, so it no longer silently matches nothing when a field's stored type has changed.

1_26_0.tagline: Browse Open VSX for a theme without leaving the window, or hand the app a .vsix and get back both your editor's exact colours and an app palette derived from them.

openVsxBrowser.title: Browse and install themes from Open VSX
openVsxBrowser.body: A new Extensions panel in the right dock — search the registry, see what each theme is (icon, author, licence, downloads, how many variants it contributes), and install and apply it in one click. Installed themes are checked for updates, and an update never overwrites a palette you have edited.

vscodeThemeImport.title: Import a VS Code colour theme
vscodeThemeImport.body: Settings → Appearance's Import theme… now also accepts a .vsix package or a bare *-color-theme.json. The editor gets the theme itself — tokenColors and all — and the rest of the app gets a palette derived from it, landing as an editable custom theme rather than an approximation.

1_25_0.tagline: Cells open already formatted, a document unfolds to the bottom in one click, forty rows go in as pasted JSON, and the workspace finally points at the tab you are actually looking at.

autoFormat.title: Cells open already formatted
autoFormat.body: Settings → Editor gains a switch per content type — JSON, XML and SQL — so a column of JSON blobs opens unfolded without your XML being reflowed too. It refuses any reformat that would change the value rather than only its whitespace, so opening a row and saving it can never rewrite a number behind your back.

expandAll.title: Unfold every nested object at once
expandAll.body: A chevron beside each card's field count opens (or closes) every nested object in that document at any depth, and the grid footer carries the same pair for the whole page. The aggregation preview has it too. Neither one rewrites your "expand nested values by default" preference.

pasteRowsJson.title: Paste rows as JSON — bulk insert on the SQL drivers
pasteRowsJson.body: One object is one row, an array is many, and the backend turns either into one multi-row INSERT per bind-ceiling chunk inside a single transaction. Keys are matched against the real catalogue before they can become identifiers, and a row whose column set differs from the first is refused rather than silently defaulted.

queryThisTable.title: "Query this table…" on the level people right-click
queryThisTable.body: A table or view in the schema tree opens a query editor already scoped to that relation's connection and database, seeded with SELECT * FROM <table> LIMIT 100. The entry existed one and two levels up and stopped short of the table you were looking at.

focusFollowsTab.title: The workspace follows the focused tab
focusFollowsTab.body: With a MySQL and a MongoDB connection both live, clicking a MySQL table and pressing + opened the editor against MongoDB. Focus now is the focused tab's connection, derived in one place — and the window title, Pulse, the AI panel, Saved Queries and the tree highlight all follow it.

fasterEnvironmentSwitch.title: Switching environments stops waiting on the network
fasterEnvironmentSwitch.body: The destination environment is handed the backend before a single outgoing pool is asked to close, so you are looking at — and working in — the new environment while the old one tears down behind it. The inert overlay that used to seal the tree and tabs is gone outright.

mysqlBackslash.title: Copied SQL no longer eats backslashes on MySQL
mysqlBackslash.body: "Copy row as ▸ INSERT/UPDATE" quoted strings by doubling ' and never touched \, so DOMAIN\user pasted back into MySQL came out as DOMAINuser. The clipboard generator now escapes \ the way the dump path always did.

1_24_0.tagline: A shared origin no longer hands you all or nothing — tick the parts you want — and a MongoDB database can finally be dropped, from a database node that single-connection trees never had.

originScope.title: Pick what you pull from a shared origin
originScope.body: A published file carries three independent things — connections, the environments that group them, and the JSON Schema library with its column bindings — and Settings → Origins now subscribes to each separately, per origin. One document, no more connections-only second file drifting out of step with the first.

mongoDatabases.title: MongoDB databases can be created and dropped
mongoDatabases.body: "Drop database…" was gated on CREATE DATABASE support, so MongoDB — which has no such command because the server does not store an empty database — could not delete a full one either. Creating asks for the first collection too, the same pair Compass asks for.

databaseNode.title: A single-database connection has a database node
databaseNode.body: A profile with a database set showed no database node at all, so "Drop database…" existed nowhere while "New database" sat in the connection's menu. Both modes now render the same menu: MySQL and MongoDB merge the schema into it, Postgres and SQL Server grow the level above public/dbo.

dropGuard.title: Dropping a database asks the right question
dropGuard.body: It had been reading ui.confirmDestructive — reasonable for a row you can re-insert, never meant to mean "drop a database on one menu click". It uses confirmIrreversible now, and all four engines that disagree about dropping the database you are connected to are handled rather than three left to fail.

emptyServer.title: A server with no databases says so
emptyServer.body: It rendered literally nothing — no row, no sentence — which reads as a connection that failed rather than a server that is empty. The tree now tells the two reasons apart: a server with nothing in it offers "New database", a tree hidden by the visible-databases subset offers the picker.

1_23_0.tagline: A script of several statements now shows every grid it produced, MongoDB query tabs get an editor that actually knows the shell, and the app's dialogs stop borrowing the operating system's.

multiResults.title: Every statement that returns rows gets its own grid
multiResults.body: Run ten SELECTs — or ten .find calls — and a strip above the results picks which one is on screen: #1 · 120 rows, #2 · 8 rows. SQL Server's extra result sets, which were being fetched and discarded, arrive too. The 50 000-row cap is now a budget the whole batch shares.

mongoEditor.title: MongoDB query tabs have their own editor language
mongoEditor.body: Shell syntax highlighting, // as the comment Ctrl+/ inserts, and completion that follows the chain: db. offers collections, a collection offers the methods the backend accepts as runnable snippets, and an argument list offers field names plus the operators that fit the call.

mongoComments.title: A comment above a MongoDB statement no longer breaks it
mongoComments.body: A // note on the line above was rejected with 'statements must start with db.' — and, worse, hid the statement from the write guard, so a commented deleteMany({}) slipped past the whole-collection-delete refusal the MCP connector applies at every tier. Both comment forms are skipped now, by one helper the guard shares.

dialogTiers.title: Dialogs and tab chips, redesigned
dialogTiers.body: Three anatomies instead of a hand-copied header rail per dialog: a compact prompt for confirms, a panel for forms, and a full workbench for Settings, the connection manager and Documentation. The active tab chip now merges into the panel below it instead of floating over a trench.

inAppConfirm.title: No more of the operating system's own prompts
inAppConfirm.body: The ten places that froze the window on a native confirm — dropping a database, importing SQL, rebuilding an index — now show a themed in-app dialog, with the same wording and the same type-to-confirm gate they had before.

gridClipping.title: The results grid stops hiding its last rows
gridClipping.body: Dropped onto a line that already held a header, the grid hung below its container by exactly the header's height and the panel clipped the overhang — the final rows were unreachable and no scrollbar said so. Measured at 48px on the reported case.

1_22_0.tagline: HuginnDB has an assistant now — local-first, read-only, off until you switch it on: it answers about your database from what it actually read, and never runs a write.

aiPanel.title: The assistant panel, in the right dock
aiPanel.body: A third occupant beside Saved Queries and Pulse, with a conversation kept per connection and nothing written to disk. Anything it proposes opens in a query tab — it never runs a statement for you.

aiTwoSwitches.title: Two switches decide what leaves your machine
aiTwoSwitches.body: Settings → AI: where inference runs is a trust level you declare, and whether rows may enter the context is separate and per connection. Both off on every existing profile; an untrusted endpoint sees names, types, indexes and EXPLAIN output only.

aiAssisted.title: Explain a statement, document a table, write the SQL
aiAssisted.body: Four jobs whose context HuginnDB assembles itself, one model call each — so they work on a model far too small for a tool loop. Right-click a statement or a table, or use the wand in the composer.

aiAgent.title: Agent mode looks things up on its own
aiAgent.body: It lists the tables, describes the ones it needs and answers from what it read — only on a model the endpoint check measured as tool-capable. Every call, and the row count that came back, lands in the Console.

mongoNestedFilter.title: MongoDB: filter on a nested field
mongoNestedFilter.body: The advanced filter's field control is now a searchable combobox of the nested paths in the page you are looking at, typed and labelled — pick customData.format, or type a path only older documents carry.

originCredentials.title: A rotated password no longer breaks a shared origin
originCredentials.body: The publisher can push a corrected connection without walking through the origin editor, and a consumer can keep their own password for one connection until the origin publishes a different one.

1_21_0.tagline: MCP connections are now managed from inside the app — pick what's exposed, install with one click — plus pipeline stage insert/duplicate, a grid that confirms your writes, and reliability fixes for very large MongoDB collections.

mcpConnections.title: Pick which connections your AI client can reach
mcpConnections.body: Exposure is now a checkbox in Settings → MCP instead of a uuid list in the client's config file, and every tool takes a connection by name — no more copying ids around.

mcpSetup.title: MCP setup in one click
mcpSetup.body: Claude Desktop installs the connector from a downloadable .mcpb bundle, and Settings → MCP can register it with Claude Code directly — no more hand-editing JSON config files.

aggregationStages.title: Insert and duplicate aggregation stages
aggregationStages.body: Add a stage exactly where it belongs in the pipeline instead of dragging it up from the bottom, and duplicate a tuned $match or $lookup instead of retyping it.

gridWrites.title: The grid confirms your writes
gridWrites.body: A short pulse marks a cell or field once its edit is saved and reloaded, MongoDB documents can now be typed by hand instead of only imported from a file, and a new button fits every column into the visible width.

mongoReliability.title: Large MongoDB collections stay responsive
mongoReliability.body: Field inference no longer hangs on a huge or time-series collection, filtered counts are capped instead of running for minutes, and the list view is now virtualized like the table view already was.

designRefresh.title: A ground-up pass on the design system
designRefresh.body: Checkboxes, buttons, tooltips, native dropdowns, spinners, and focus rings are unified across the app into shared, consistent primitives — plus dozens of small color, radius, and spacing fixes.

1_20_0.tagline: Introducing HuginnDB Pulse — live server health for MySQL and MongoDB, right next to your workspace — plus in-place editing for shared origins, aggregation autocomplete, and a project-wide performance pass.

pulse.title: Introducing HuginnDB Pulse
pulse.body: How is the server doing right now, and how has it been doing lately? Live vital signs, the slowest statements (with a runnable EXPLAIN plan), biggest tables, active sessions, and unused indexes — for MySQL and MongoDB, docked next to your workspace or expanded into a window of its own. Turn on the history sampler per connection to answer "was this slow yesterday too?" — everything is also reachable read-only over MCP.

originEditing.title: Fix a shared origin's connection in place
originEditing.body: Correcting a stale password published through a shared origin no longer means duplicating the connection, editing the copy, republishing, and cleaning up the orphaned original. The origin's own publisher can now edit a published connection — password included — in the same dialog, same id, and republish when ready.

aggregationAutocomplete.title: Compass-style autocomplete in the aggregation editor
aggregationAutocomplete.body: Typing $ in a stage body now suggests the source collection's field names alongside operators, and $lookup offers collection and field names for from/localField/foreignField.

performance.title: A project-wide performance pass
performance.body: Dozens of file-and-line-identified fixes across the schema tree, the data grid, the SQL editor and the shell remove unnecessary re-renders and redundant disk writes — including the fix for a 10k-row table degrading to unusable in list mode.

cliEnvironments.title: The CLI now follows your environments
cliEnvironments.body: Connecting via --connect-profile or an ad-hoc --host/--uri switches to (or reuses) the right environment automatically, and reuses an already-saved profile instead of always minting a new ephemeral one.

1_19_0.tagline: A full editor for what a shared origin publishes, the keyboard-shortcut system rebuilt from the ground up, and MongoDB gets index and collection management.

sharedOriginEditor.title: A full editor for what a shared origin publishes
sharedOriginEditor.body: Edit which connections a shared origin publishes and how their passwords travel, its environments, and its JSON Schema library — all from one screen, with a preview that shows exactly what every consumer's next sync will see before you publish.

keyboardShortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts, rebuilt from the ground up
keyboardShortcuts.body: Bind more than one key to an action, chain chord sequences like Mod+K then Mod+S, and see exactly where a shortcut can fire (grid, editor, tree, or everywhere). The catalogue grew from 8 actions to 25, and Settings → Shortcuts now searches by action or by key.

mongoIndexDdl.title: MongoDB gets index and collection management
mongoIndexDdl.body: Create, hide and drop indexes, and drop or rename collections, straight from the query editor — and an AI client can now do the same over MCP with two new tools, at the same write-policy tier as any other schema change.

pinnedColumns.title: Pin columns to the left edge of the grid
pinnedColumns.body: Excel-style column pinning in the data browser — click the pin icon in any header to keep it in view while you scroll through a wide result set. Persisted per table, like column widths.

schemaSearch.title: The schema search now looks at every open connection
schemaSearch.body: The filter used to silently search only whichever connection was selected — reported by several users. It now searches every live connection at once, shows a match count per connection, and never opens new database pools just because you typed a letter.

connectionProvenance.title: Connections show where they came from
connectionProvenance.body: The connection manager and the MCP panel both split into Local and Shared-by-origin, with a read-only section per origin — and the MCP panel adds bulk write-policy buttons so you can set Read-only/Data/Full for a whole list at once.

1_18_0.tagline: A notification system built for the app, full view management over the MCP connector, and a project-wide performance and reliability pass.

notifications.title: A notification system of its own
notifications.body: Every toast is now rendered by HuginnDB itself, not the library's stock defaults — a themed card, duplicate notifications collapsed into one with a counter, a history behind a bell in the toolbar, and a progress card for imports and exports that outlive the dialog that started them.

mcpViews.title: Views over the MCP connector: read, edit and delete
mcpViews.body: An AI client can now read a view's definition, create or redefine one, and drop it, on all five drivers — including MongoDB's stored aggregation pipelines. Same write policy as any other DDL change: a connection needs full write access.

performance.title: Internal: a faster, more reliable app under the hood
performance.body: Fixed a multi-second launch freeze caused by re-hashing every shared-origin secret on the main thread, and a SQL Server bug that hung the schema explorer forever loading columns. A project-wide pass also removed duplicated logic across the Rust backend and the frontend — same behavior, less code to drift.

bugFixes.title: A round of issue and bug fixes
bugFixes.body: Dropping a MongoDB "view" whose name matched a real collection could wipe every document in it — now refused. Blank-named MongoDB indexes, bulk updates on MySQL BIT columns, and a dozen smaller inconsistencies (locale formatting, import numbering, missing translations) are fixed too.

docsSections.title: The documentation viewer now has sections
docsSections.body: Each guide opens on a cover with a card per section, the sidebar is a tree derived straight from the markdown, and in-document links actually jump to their target now.

1_17_0.tagline: Your editor now understands JSON Schemas — and a runaway query can no longer take down the app.

jsonSchemas.title: A JSON Schema library, bound to your columns
jsonSchemas.body: Keep a library of named schemas and bind each one to a column (by connection, database, table and column, with globs and a most-specific-wins cascade). A bound column gets real completion, enum suggestions, hover documentation and underlined violations in the cell editor — in the modal and the docked panel, on every driver including MongoDB and SQL Server. "Create from this value" drafts one from the document you're already looking at. Validation never blocks a save: the database stays the authority.

querySafety.title: A runaway SELECT can no longer crash the app
querySafety.body: A hand-typed query with no LIMIT/TOP over a huge table used to buffer the entire result in memory and could take the whole app down with an out-of-memory crash. Every ad-hoc read path now caps itself at 50,000 rows and shows a "truncated" badge instead, and the data grid renders rows through a real virtualizer rather than one DOM row per result.

originEnvironments.title: Shared origins can now sync a whole environment
originEnvironments.body: Point an origin at an environment export instead of a plain profile bundle and it keeps a read-only mirror environment in sync on every pull — created on first sync, refreshed after, and reported as vanished (never silently deleted) if the file disappears.

importProgress.title: Bulk imports get a progress bar and one-click conflict resolution
importProgress.body: The profile/environment import dialogs now show "N of total" while a large import runs off the main thread, and "Mark all as: Rename/Overwrite/Skip" resolves a whole conflict list at once instead of one row at a time.

columnReorder.title: Reorder columns in the MySQL structure editor
columnReorder.body: Move a column up or down without dropping and re-adding it — MySQL's MODIFY COLUMN / ADD COLUMN … FIRST|AFTER makes this possible; the other drivers don't have an equivalent ALTER.

1_16_0.tagline: MongoDB gets a real editing surface — a Compass-style aggregation editor for views and a full index manager — plus a connection-reliability fix for long-idle multi-database sessions, and a visual refresh: a new logo and light/dark pairs for every built-in theme.

mongoAggregation.title: Edit MongoDB views with a Compass-style aggregation editor
mongoAggregation.body: "New aggregation…" on any collection opens a scratch pipeline, and "Edit pipeline…" on any view loads its stored one — both in a Stages view (one card per stage, its own sample output) or a single Text editor, with export as a mongosh call, a bare pipeline, or a db.createView(…) snippet. $out and $merge are refused before they ever reach the server.

mongoIndexes.title: A real index manager for MongoDB
mongoIndexes.body: "Indexes…" on any collection opens the real catalogue — create, hide, replace and drop — showing each index's size and how many operations it's served since the counter was last reset, so you can spot the ones nobody queries. Editing is a drop plus a create, since MongoDB can't alter an index in place.

connectionReliability.title: Multi-database connections stay usable after sitting idle
connectionReliability.body: A server-style connection (Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server) used to stop browsing a database after a few idle minutes even though the tree still showed it connected — the reaped child pool behind it is now reopened transparently on the next click. The huginndb-mcp connector also stopped misreporting a legitimate null result as an empty reply.

brandIdentity.title: A real brand identity, not just an icon
brandIdentity.body: The old raven/rune mark is gone — a new comic logo now leads the About card, the launch splash, and the medallion every empty screen shares (connections tree, console, saved queries, an empty result set), each with its own glyph as a corner badge. Every installer icon, from the Windows taskbar down to Android/iOS, was regenerated from it, and the dev tab finally has a favicon.

themePairs.title: Every built-in theme now has a light/dark twin
themePairs.body: Summer Dark and Neon Light join the roster, and High Contrast now works in both directions — ten themes total, each with a real counterpart instead of stranding you on a HuginnDB default. The 26-colour editor in Preferences → Appearance is also split into four labelled sections (Surfaces, Actions & brand, Status colours, Borders & focus) so related tokens read together.

1_15_0.tagline: Environments get a face of their own, Linux finally gets installers straight off the releases page, and two rough edges — fold state shared where it shouldn't be, and a restart button that went silent — are filed down.

environmentAvatars.title: Give an environment its own image
environmentAvatars.body: The create/rename dialog now takes a custom avatar: pick a file, or drop one on the preview. It replaces the initials everywhere the environment appears — the rail, the workspace picker, the status-bar switcher — which is what finally tells "Cliente A" and "Cliente B" apart at a glance. Whatever you pick is cropped square and downscaled, and it travels inside the environment itself. The rail's label is slightly larger too, and the active one now reads in bold.

linuxBuilds.title: Linux downloads on the releases page
linuxBuilds.body: Every tagged release now attaches an x86_64 .deb and .AppImage next to the Windows installer, so Linux no longer means building from source. The README covers both, including which glibc the AppImage is built against.

independentFolds.title: Folds stay where you left them
independentFolds.body: Collapsing a connection group inside the connections manager no longer reaches behind the dialog and collapses it in the Schema tree as well. Every surface now starts from the same remembered arrangement but folds independently from there, and "remember" still writes through for the next one you open.

restartFeedback.title: "Restart now" shows it heard you
restartFeedback.body: The install button used to keep looking idle and clickable through the whole MCP-sidecar check that runs before an update installs. It now disables itself and shows a spinner the instant you click, and a second click can no longer queue a second install.

1_14_0.tagline: The command palette becomes a real launcher, the window shell reorganizes around an activity bar, environments get their own rail, and themes travel between machines.

paletteLauncher.title: The palette is a real launcher now
paletteLauncher.body: Ctrl/Cmd+K indexes thirteen groups — every preference and shortcut, every doc, open tabs, connections, environments, tables and views across all connected connections, saved queries and history — scored and ranked, with mode prefixes (>, @, #, ?, :) and a "Recently used" section. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P opens it in actions-only mode.

activityBarShell.title: A redesigned window shell
activityBarShell.body: Schema, Saved and Console are no longer draggable dockview panels: Console docks to the bottom, Saved collapses from a right-hand activity bar, and the workspace is a fixed island with its own header. Every panel animates open and closed, and new toggle buttons show or hide each one independently.

environmentRail.title: An environment rail
environmentRail.body: The left activity bar is now a Discord/Teams-style column of environment avatars — initials over each environment's accent colour — replacing the old icon picker. Click one to switch and open Schema in one gesture; right-click for rename/delete.

themeTransfer.title: Import and export themes
themeTransfer.body: Settings → Appearance can now save the active theme to a JSON file and load one back as a brand-new custom theme. A new "Summer" built-in theme joins the set, and environments can carry their own theme override.

columnFit.title: Double-click a column edge to fit it
columnFit.body: The data grid's column resize handle now double-click-fits a column to its widest visible value (Ctrl/Cmd-click fits every column at once), and the toolbar's responsive collapse keeps filters and actions usable on a narrow pane.

1_13_0.tagline: A fifth engine — Microsoft SQL Server — a connection footprint that is finally bounded, visible and yours to set, and a list view that edits on every driver.

sqlServer.title: Microsoft SQL Server
sqlServer.body: The fifth driver: connect (SSH tunnels, named instances, Windows authentication on Windows builds), browse schemas/tables/views/indexes, run T-SQL, and edit, insert, delete and bulk-update rows. The structure editor and .sql export stay read-only for now.

connectionFootprint.title: Far fewer connections
connectionFootprint.body: Browsing a multi-database server no longer opens an unbounded pool per database: they are capped, reused and closed after five minutes idle. Cross-database search stops flooding the server, MongoDB takes the same budget as everyone else, and a "too many connections" error now says so — with what HuginnDB itself is holding.

connectionSettings.title: A budget you set, per server
connectionSettings.body: Settings → Connections shows live how many pools are open and lets you set the allowance for a whole server — shared by every connection and database view reaching it — globally or on a single connection.

listEditor.title: The list view now edits
listEditor.body: Double-click a value to edit it in place, fold and unfold nested objects and arrays, and on MongoDB change a field's BSON type, add fields or remove them. It is no longer MongoDB-only: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite get it too.

mcpPools.title: One budget, MCP included
mcpPools.body: The huginndb-mcp connector can borrow the app's pools instead of opening its own, so however many AI clients are configured the machine keeps one budget per server — and their activity shows up live in the Console.

1_12_1.tagline: Export and import get a proper redesign — connection- and database-level dialogs, plus grid-toolbar shortcuts — alongside a bulk update tool and a reworked structure editor.

exportImport.title: Export/import redesign
exportImport.body: "Export database…" is now a dialog covering one or more databases (and, per database, which tables) into a single combined .sql file; "Import .sql…" previews the statement count and lets multi-DB connections pick a target. The grid toolbar gained its own "Export data" (full table or query results) and, for MongoDB, "Import JSON…".

bulkUpdate.title: Bulk update
bulkUpdate.body: Update every row/document matching a filter in one round trip, for all four drivers — reuses the grid's advanced-filter builder for the match side and previews the exact statement before running.

structureEditor.title: Categorised type picker
structureEditor.body: The structure editor's column type combo is now grouped by category (Integers/Real/Text/Date & time/Binary/Other) with its own length/precision field and MySQL unsigned/zerofill checkboxes, plus a redesigned columns table matching the app's own grid look.

tableRename.title: Renaming a table works again
tableRename.body: The Name field is editable when editing a table, and applying a rename updates every open tab's title instead of leaving the old name showing.

1_12_0.tagline: Environments group your connections into named, switchable sessions — with shared origins to sync them across a team, connections now living in the schema tree, and a redesigned query run experience.

environments.title: Environments
environments.body: A new level above connections: a named set of connections with its own tabs, pane layout and reconnect behaviour, switchable from a topbar selector — one environment per client instead of one window per client.

sharedOrigins.title: Shared origins
sharedOrigins.body: An environment can sync its connections — and their passwords — from a shared config file on the network, so joining a team means entering a passphrase once instead of configuring every connection by hand.

connectionsInTree.title: Connections live in the schema tree
connectionsInTree.body: The tree now starts with folders and connections as its top two levels, so opening a second server is a click in the same window instead of a trip through a separate menu.

filterSelected.title: Filter by the selected rows
filterSelected.body: Select rows in the data grid, right-click a column, and filter the rest of the table down to (or excluding) exactly those values — deduplicated, and working on every driver, MongoDB included.

queryFeedback.title: Redesigned query feedback
queryFeedback.body: A live run timer, a bigger default editor/results split, and a searchable query history with a one-click "run again" replace the old bare running/finished label.

neonTheme.title: Neon, a new dark theme
neonTheme.body: A near-black theme built around a signature neon green accent, with cyan/amber/pink picked to match — a fresh coat for anyone tired of the two defaults.

1_11_0.tagline: The app reconnects on launch and opens big tables almost instantly, with a cleaner single-bar grid toolbar, a MongoDB list view and true floating windows.

reconnect.title: Reconnect on launch
reconnect.body: A new General preference (on by default) reopens the connections that were live when you last closed the app — using the credentials already in the OS keychain — restoring the same focused connection, tab and pane layout you left behind.

fastOpen.title: Big tables open almost instantly
fastOpen.body: Rows now render as soon as the query returns instead of waiting on an exact COUNT(*); whole-table totals come from the engine's own statistics as an approximate ~N, so multi-million-row tables no longer stall on open.

toolbar.title: A single, cleaner table toolbar
toolbar.body: The table toolbar is now one Compass-style bar — search grows to fill the width, Insert sits beside it, and pagination, zoom and elapsed time move to the right — dropping the old bottom status strip and the duplicated row count for more grid space.

mongoList.title: MongoDB list view
mongoList.body: MongoDB collections gain a table/list toggle: list mode renders each document as a card with pretty-printed nested objects and arrays, instead of forcing endless horizontal scrolling and one-line JSON blobs in table mode.

floatWindow.title: Float a tab into a real window
floatWindow.body: "Float in new window" now opens a genuine, independent OS window hosting just that one tab — movable anywhere on the desktop — instead of a floating panel trapped inside the workspace pane.

1_10_0.tagline: View editing lands in the schema explorer, alongside fully customizable keyboard shortcuts and quicker grid actions.

viewsEditor.title: Views can now be created, edited and dropped
viewsEditor.body: The schema explorer's new "Edit view…" tab pairs a full Monaco SQL editor with a live preview grid and a read-only DDL pane — no more hand-writing CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW.

betweenFilter.title: A `between` operator in the Advanced Filter
betweenFilter.body: Filter an inclusive range in a single condition — on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and MongoDB — instead of stacking a >= row and a <= row.

shortcuts.title: Customizable keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Settings → Shortcuts lets you rebind six actions — open settings, command palette, tab switcher, refresh, run query and the new expand-cell shortcut — with collision checks and a reset-all button.

gridQuickActions.title: Faster data-grid actions
gridQuickActions.body: Click a selected cell to reveal an expand icon for a quick full-value view, and use Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V to copy and paste cell values directly — no more double-clicking just to read.

1_9_0.tagline: Your AI tools can now write to your databases — safely, on your terms, one connection at a time.

mcpWrite.title: MCP connector write-mode
mcpWrite.body: The huginndb-mcp connector, read-only until now, can insert, update and delete rows — and change schema — through your AI tool. New insert_row, update_cell and delete_rows tools, plus writes via run_query.

mcpPolicy.title: Per-connection write policy, with an audit log
mcpPolicy.body: Each connection is read-only by default; raise it to 'data' or 'full' in Settings → MCP, per connection, with changes taking effect immediately. Whole-table UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE are refused, and every write is recorded in mcp-audit.log.

advancedFilter.title: Advanced per-column filter
advancedFilter.body: A new filter button in the table toolbar opens a builder: add conditions per column (contains, starts/ends with, >, <, equals, is null…), all combined with AND and applied on the server. Type-aware, and works across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and MongoDB.

1_8_0.tagline: MongoDB catches up: multi-database connections and the MCP connector both get real driver parity.

security.title: Security panel works on multi-database connections
security.body: Opening the Security tab on a MongoDB connection with no preselected database no longer errors — it now lists users and privileges across the whole cluster.

mcpMongo.title: MCP no longer blocks MongoDB reads
mcpMongo.body: `run_query` used a SQL-only read-only check that rejected every mongosh statement by default. It now recognises MongoDB reads correctly, the same way the desktop query editor already did.

mcpMongoDatabase.title: MCP tools can target a MongoDB database
mcpMongoDatabase.body: list_tables, describe_table, list_indexes, browse_table (schema) and run_query (database) can now target a specific database on a multi-database MongoDB connection — the same thing expanding a database in the explorer does, just from your AI tool.

columnTypes.title: Real column types instead of generic "bson"
columnTypes.body: Query and browse results now show each column's actual BSON type (int, string, date, objectId, …) instead of one generic label — useful for you and for AI tools using the MCP connector.

collectionSize.title: Collection size in the explorer
collectionSize.body: MongoDB collections now show an on-disk size, fetched in a single batched call instead of skipping it.

1_7_0.tagline: Bring your databases to your AI tools — HuginnDB now speaks the Model Context Protocol.

connector.title: MCP connector for AI tools
connector.body: A new headless `huginndb-mcp` server lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients inspect your databases — schema, tables, indexes, sample rows and server info — using the connections you already saved.

safety.title: Read-only and opt-in by design
safety.body: Nothing is exposed until you name a connection, queries are read-only, passwords stay in your OS keychain, and a row cap keeps results in check. See docs/MCP.md to wire up your client.

1_6_0.tagline: A top-to-bottom interface overhaul — the same keyboard-first HuginnDB, sharper in every corner.

design.title: Refined design system
design.body: A consistent colour, type and elevation scale, clearer focus rings, and semantic success / warning tokens that follow your theme.

grid.title: Keyboard-navigable data grid
grid.body: Move the active cell with the arrow keys, select rows with visible checkboxes, and read numbers in aligned tabular figures.

schema.title: Redesigned schema tree
schema.body: The open table is marked so you always know where you are, column types are colour-coded, and rows load behind a subtle skeleton.

editor.title: Sharper query editor & command palette
editor.body: A visible Run button with its shortcut, a flagship cell editor with content-type badges, and a polished command palette with hints.

chrome.title: Clearer status & themed tooltips
chrome.body: Lost connections are unmissable with one-click reconnect, and tooltips across the chrome now match your theme instead of the OS.
